newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit stays in range, seen led by dollar/majors.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit stays in range, seen led by dollar/majors.

text.p: The ringgit showed little movement after some early morning fluctuations as market focused on dollar/majors, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said apart from a bout of mild dollar/ringgit selling in the afternoon, the market was extremely quiet.
"Dollar/ringgit moved in a 15 point range today. Dollar is strong after the Fed decided to keep rates steady and the ringgit is tracking the trend," a local bank dealer said.
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee, at a meeting on Tuesday, decided to keep interest rates unchanged.
In early trading the ringgit was volatile, but in a range as month-end commercial dollar demand from Kuala Lumpur was matched by Japanese buying.
"Some Japanese started selling as soon as dollar/ringgit touched 2.5020," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.
She said strong commercial demand for the dollar from Kuala Lumpur had earlier lifted the ringgit from 2.50 level.
A dealer with a U.S. bank in Singapore said the near-term strategy was to play the range for lack of new trading factors.
At 0900 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5009/14 per dollar against 2.5010/15 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
